sections.html: Moenkhausia hemigrammoides are very lively fish that constantly play with each other and rush through the aquarium in lightning-fast turns. The fish grow to about 4 cm in length (in nature the size of adult animals is between 2.1 and 3.3 cm, measured without caudal fin) and are therefore a real enrichment of the aquarium, even if they are not very conspicuous in colour.

Until recently, Moenkhausia hemigrammoides was thought to occur only in the Guyana countries. A study published in September 2019 describes for the first time its occurrence in Colombia (rivers Ariari and Inirida, both tributaries to the Rio Guaviare in the upper Orinoco basin), which makes the occurrence of the species in Venezuela very likely.

From Venezuela, "feather tetras" were recently received. This is what tetras with a striking black stripe in the anal fin, accompanied by a white line in front of it, used to be called. However, the term "feather tetra" is alternatively used for species of the genus Hemiodus or Hyphessobrycon copelandi. These fish were first identified as Hemigrammus unilineatus.

Hemigrammus unilineatus is the type species of the genus Hemigrammus. It has a double, namely Moenkhausia hemigrammoides. The only externally visible difference between the two species is the lateral line. In Hemigrammus this line runs over half the body length (Hemi: half, grammus: drawn), in Moenkhausia it runs over the whole body length. This feature can be seen on sharp photos.

Hemigrammus unilineatus occurs in the Guyana countries and also in large parts of Brazil, Venezuela, Colombia and Bolivia. The imported fish have a complete lateral line, so they are Moenkhausia hemigrammoides.
